title: Guidelines: when to use Status Page vs KB banner vs Console alert (with templates + examples)
creator: Talia Benson
project: CS & Support Escalation Playbook Refresh + Known-Issues Sprint (2026-02)
description:
Goal
Define clear, repeatable guidance for choosing between (a) Status Page incident/maintenance posts, (b) docs-site (Help Center) “Known Issue” banners, and (c) in-app Console alerts. This is meant to reduce inconsistent customer messaging during incidents and reduce repeat tickets by making the right workaround discoverable.

Audience
- Support/CS: deciding what to tell customers and where to point them
- SRE/On-call: deciding whether an issue is “status-worthy” vs “workaround-worthy”
- Docs/DevEx: implementing banners and keeping copy consistent
- PM/Design: ensuring user-facing messaging is scoped, accurate, and not alarmist

Non-goals
- Redefine incident severity rubric (covered in escalation playbook)
- Create brand/visual system work beyond standard components
- Decide contract/SLA language

Decision framework (single source of truth)
Use this as a quick decision tree. If more than one channel applies, the order is: Status Page (canonical for outages) → Console alert (high salience for active users) → KB banner (workaround discoverability + deflection). Avoid posting contradictory timelines/cause statements across channels.

1) Status Page: when to post
Post to Status Page when the issue meets ANY of:
- Broad service health impact: multi-customer or multi-tenant degradation/outage
- Measurable SLO impact: sustained elevated error rate/latency in a region/model tier that affects multiple customers
- Safety/compliance impact: incident affecting audit logs delivery expectations for multiple enterprise accounts (or risk of data integrity)
- Customer trust risk: high-visibility customer impact likely to be detected externally (e.g., social, community) even if not yet widely reported
- Planned maintenance: any maintenance window with potential customer-observable impact, even if “low risk”

Do NOT use Status Page for:
- Customer-specific configuration issues (DNS, IdP config, webhook TLS chain)
- Single-account quota/limits confusion unless systemic
- “Known limitation” that has a stable workaround and does not represent platform health regression

Status Page content rules
- Keep statements verifiable: what’s impacted, when it started, mitigation in progress
- No speculative root cause (“likely” OK only if explicitly framed as preliminary)
- Include a link to a KB article ONLY if the workaround is validated and safe for broad use
- Keep timelines consistent with SRE incident updates; Support should not introduce new ETAs

2) Console alert: when to show
Use Console alert when:
- Customers actively in product need immediate, contextual guidance to reduce harm or avoid retries/overuse
- The issue is scoped to a subset that can be targeted (region, product tier, specific endpoint)
- There is a clear customer action that improves outcomes (e.g., “use eu-central temporarily”, “reduce batch size”, “retry with jitter”) and we want it to show up where they operate
- We want to reduce inbound tickets while the incident is active (especially for Hosted self-serve users)

Do NOT use Console alert when:
- No customer action exists (pure informational), and Status Page already covers it
- Message would cause panic or churn without actionable next step
- Content includes sensitive account details

Console alert UX guidance
- Title: 55–75 chars, concrete and scoped (region/product)
- Include 1–2 bullets max + 1 primary link (Status Page or KB)
- Avoid “investigating” with no action; if no action, prefer Status Page-only
- Targeting: region + endpoint where possible; default to global only with SRE sign-off

3) KB banner (Help Center / docs site): when to use
Use KB banner when:
- There is a validated workaround or mitigation that Support wants to be copy/paste-ready
- The issue is recurring or likely to generate repeat tickets (“known-issues sprint” candidates)
- The issue may not be status-worthy but is confusing enough to cause escalations (e.g., 429 header mismatch, streaming reconnect behavior)
- We need to set expectations with guardrails (“temporary”, “when to escalate”, “what to collect”)

Do NOT use KB banner when:
- Workaround is unverified or risky to recommend broadly
- The issue is purely transient and already resolved; instead update the KB article without a banner
- The issue is actually an outage → use Status Page as primary

KB banner placement guidance
- Place banner at:
  - Known Issues landing page (always, if tagged “active”)
  - The relevant API/SDK troubleshooting page (if the issue maps cleanly)
  - The specific endpoint docs page only if it’s high-volume (avoid banner fatigue)
- Recency: banner must include “Last updated” and a “Current status” link (Status Page if incident is active)

Channel combinations (most common)
A) Outage/degradation with workaround
- Status Page: YES (canonical)
- Console alert: YES if there is customer action to reduce impact
- KB banner: YES if workaround is stable and ticket-deflecting

B) Recurring issue with workaround (no service health incident)
- Status Page: NO
- Console alert: Maybe (only if issue is currently spiking and there’s immediate action)
- KB banner: YES

C) Customer-specific misconfiguration
- Status Page: NO
- Console alert: NO
- KB banner: Maybe (only if it’s a common pattern, phrased generically)

Copy templates (approved structure)
Template 1: Status Page incident update (degradation)
- Title: “[Region] Degraded performance for [Product/Endpoint]”
- Body (3 bullets max):
  - Impact: what users see (timeouts, elevated 5xx, truncated streams)
  - Scope: region/endpoints/models/tier (avoid customer names)
  - Mitigation: what we’re doing + any safe customer action
- Footer: “Next update by: <time>” (align to comms cadence from SLA policy)

Template 2: Console alert (actionable)
- Title: “Issues with [endpoint] in [region] — recommended workaround”
- Body:
  - “If you see <symptom>, try <action>.”
  - “If still failing, contact Support with: request IDs, region, model, SDK version.”
  - Link: Status Page OR KB article (choose one)

Template 3: KB banner (known issue)
- Tag: ACTIVE | MONITORING | RESOLVED (banners only for ACTIVE/MONITORING)
- Banner copy:
  - “Known issue: <short symptom>. Workaround available.”
  - “Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD”
  - CTA: “View workaround” → KB article
  - Secondary link (optional): Status Page (only if incident active)

Examples (use cases from Support top issues)
Example 1: Streaming connection resets in us-east (multi-customer spike)
- Status Page: YES (service health degradation)
- Console alert: YES (recommend retry/backoff + adjust timeouts; link to Status Page)
- KB banner: YES (link to “Streaming timeouts and reconnect” workaround; include ‘when to escalate’)

Example 2: Rate-limit headers inconsistent / quota mismatch (recurring confusion)
- Status Page: NO (unless systemic outage-level)
- Console alert: NO (not time-critical)
- KB banner: YES (workaround + interpret headers; link from SDK docs)

Example 3: Audit log delivery latency elevated (enterprise expectations)
- Status Page: YES if lag impacts multiple enterprise accounts or shared pipeline backlog
- Console alert: Maybe (only for affected tiers if targeting exists)
- KB banner: YES if a safe mitigation exists (e.g., export window guidance) + escalation criteria

Example 4: Private installer upgrade stuck at migrations (customer-specific but repeatable)
- Status Page: NO (customer deployment)
- Console alert: NO
- KB banner: YES, phrased generically with diagnostics bundle steps and “contact Support before rollback” warnings

Governance / approvals
- Status Page posts: SRE on-call owner (or incident commander) approves. Support can draft but must not publish without SRE sign-off.
- Console alerts: Product/Platform on-call + Support lead approve (fast path), with Docs reviewing copy when possible.
- KB banners: Docs/DevEx owner publishes after SRE/Eng validates workaround; Support confirms ticket deflection usefulness.

Operational notes
- Single canonical link rule: Each message should point customers to ONE canonical source for ongoing updates:
  - If active incident: Status Page is canonical.
  - If not an incident: KB article is canonical.
- Avoid banner fatigue: do not stack multiple banners on a single page; prefer a single banner that links to an index filtered by tags.
- Sensitivity: do not include customer names, contract terms, internal dashboard links, or specific capacity numbers.

Deliverables
- 1-pager “Channel Decision Matrix” (this ticket)
- Copy templates (Status Page / Console / KB banner)
- 4 worked examples aligned to top Support issues
- Checklist for Support triage: “Should I request a status post? Should I request a KB banner?”

Open questions
- Do we have Console targeting by region/endpoint in the current alert system? If not, default guidance should be conservative (fewer Console alerts).
- Do we want a formal ‘MONITORING’ state on KB banners, or does that create ambiguity vs Status Page? Proposal: allow MONITORING only when Status Page is NOT active.

Requested reviewers

Templates are copy/paste-ready and avoid speculative language; include ‘last updated’ and canonical link guidance
Guidance aligns with Support comms templates and incident comms alignment doc (no conflicting update cadence)
Review sign-offs captured from SRE + Enterprise CS + Docs
